source.section: Form 540 lines 13 to 19 and 31 to 33 (PDF pages 39-40); PDF page 13 Line 18 standard deduction chart and Line 31; PDF page 75 Tax Rate Schedules; PDF page 39 Form 540 lines 7 and 9 ('X $153'); PDF page 12 Line 7 and Line 9; PDF page 14 Line 32 and the AGI Limitation Worksheet lines a to i

worked: Single, 45: wages 340,000; federal AGI = 340,000, which is 87,797 over the 252,203 limit, beyond the 62,500 range over which the stepped phase-down still leaves part of a 153 credit, so the form and the projection agree. Form 540 line 13 federal AGI = 340,000.00. Federal taxable income = 340,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 324,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtractions: none (wages need no adjustment). Form 540 line 14 = 0.00. Additions (line 16): 0.00. Line 15 = line 17 California AGI = 340,000.00 - 0.00 = 340,000.00. Line 18 California standard deduction (single, PDF page 13 chart) 5,706.00. Line 19 taxable income = 340,000.00 - 5,706.00 = 334,294.00. Tax on 334,294.00 by the projection's brackets: 11,079.00 x 1% = 110.79; 15,185.00 x 2% = 303.70; 15,188.00 x 4% = 607.52; 16,090.00 x 6% = 965.40; 15,182.00 x 8% = 1,214.56; 261,570.00 x 9.3% = 24,326.01; total 27,527.98. Line 31: Tax Rate Schedule X (PDF page 75), from its printed base, gives 27,527.98. Line 11 exemptions: 1 personal x 153 and 0 senior x 153. Federal AGI 340,000.00 is more than 252,203.00: the projection removes the personal and senior credits, line 32 = 0.00. The form's AGI Limitation Worksheet (PDF page 14) would give: c = 87,797 over 252,203.00; d = 87,797 / 2,500 rounded up = 36; e = 36 x 6 = 216; f = 1 boxes on lines 7 and 9; g = 216 x 1 = 216; h = 153; i = 153 - 216 = 0 (zero or less enters 0); line 32 = 0. Line 33 = 27,527.98 - 0.00 = 27,527.98; no other credits (lines 34 to 47 nil), line 48 = 27,527.98. State income tax = 27,527.98.
